top_story: Washington’s 4 May deployment of warships to break Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz turned a long-running coercive exchange into direct military pressure on one of the world’s most exposed shipping lanes, where hundreds of vessels were already trapped and regional energy flows were under strain. That move followed Tehran’s March warning of wider escalation after Trump threatened Iran’s power grid, showing that the current confrontation grew from reciprocal brinkmanship rather than a sudden rupture. Inside Iran, the 4 May execution of three men tied to January anti-regime protests points to a parallel effort to harden domestic control as external pressure rises, raising the likelihood that state violence will expand both at sea and at home. The emerging picture is a narrowing space for de-escalation, with Hormuz becoming both a military flashpoint and a pressure valve for Iran’s internal insecurity.
